description:
s473u member 1 (2026-09-08): PROFILE THE GATE PER FILE before building any
lever, then build only what the table licenses.

=== DONE (s473u) ===

THE BEFORE, measured on a quiet box (uptime 1.09 -> 3.67, no sibling gate),
cached core, `PCLXS_DIR=~/pclxs prove -j8 --timer Pl/t/`:
  224 files, 7720 rows, 463 s wall, 2933 CPU-s (2630 usr + 303 sys), 539 MB RSS.

UNIT PRICES on the same box:
  one pl2cl spawn (trivial file)                      0.13 CPU-s
  one sbcl run from the CACHED CORE + compile-load    0.007 CPU-s
  one sbcl run that --loads cl/pcl-runtime.lisp       2.89 CPU-s
  perl -e0                                            0.00

DECOMPOSITION (220 timed files: ~3221 pl2cl spawns, ~3106 sbcl runs):
  fixed transpile cost   3221 x 0.13 = ~419 CPU-s (14 %)
  sbcl starts from core  3106 x 0.007 = ~22 CPU-s -- SBCL START IS NOT A LEVER
  residue                             ~2400 CPU-s (82 %)

THE FINDING THE TABLE PRODUCED, and it was not the one the brief expected:
15 gate files still spelled `sbcl --noinform --non-interactive --load
cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` themselves.  They never called PCLCore::sbcl_prefix, so
the saved core built for exactly this purpose was unused and every row
recompiled the whole runtime: 2.89 CPU-s against 0.007 s.  They were the two
slowest files in the gate and 9 of the top 12 by wall:
  autoviv-01 180.8 s  local-elem-02 169.5  loop-labels-01 82.7  utf8-source-01
  77.2  our-local-01 65.6  default-underscore-01 61.1  local-elem-01 59.9
  parser2-02 56.0  local-glob-01 53.3  goto-label-01 40.8  parser2-01 37.8
  local-symref-01 32.4  loop-body-context-01 29.2  file-line-01 21.6
  errno-01 16.2
Measured ALONE at -j4: 974 CPU-s / 627 rows = 33 % of the gate's CPU for 8 % of
its rows.  They also ran on the DEFAULT 2 MB control stack rather than the
512 MB every other gate file gets -- the #324 drift that the one-prefix rule
(task #344) exists to prevent, alive in 15 files.

LEVER A (shipped in the same commit): the 15 files routed through
PCLCore::sbcl_prefix.  Measured alone at -j4: 974 -> 25.2 CPU-s, 297 -> 9.7 s
wall, the same 627 rows, all passing; scratch/s473u/tap-diff.pl against the
full BEFORE gate = ZERO row differences.  38.6x on that subset.

INSTRUMENT KEPT: tools/gate-profile.pl reads a `prove --timer` log and prints
the table (per file: wall, rows, helper calls by kind, the attribution).
GUARD: Pl/t/gate-cost-01.t row 1 fails naming every file that spells its own
runtime-source load, so the drift cannot come back silently.

=== THE SAME LEVER A SECOND TIME (s473u member 3) ===

After the first pass the top of the table was eval-01.t 153 s,
decl-ordering-02.t 143, begin-end-01.t 108, decl-ordering-01.t 103,
use-require-01.t 98, eval-named-sub-01.t 44, moo-01.t 35,
local-paren-begin-do-01.t 29 â and every one of them kept its OWN
`my $runtime = 'cl/pcl-runtime.lisp'` and ran `sbcl â¦ --load $runtime`.

THE FIRST SCAN COULD NOT SEE THEM: it looked for the literal `pcl-runtime.lisp`
ON the sbcl line, and these spell the path through a VARIABLE.  The rule had
been written about how the path is SPELLED when it is about where the COMMAND
COMES FROM.  The guard row now flags any `sbcl â¦ --load` command a gate file
builds itself (a backtick / qx / system line without @sbcl_rt), so neither
spelling can come back.  Ten files, thirteen command sites.

MEASURED, the ten alone at -j4, same 294 rows, both PASS, ZERO row differences:
**604.08 -> 27.15 CPU-s (22.2x), 235 -> 21 s wall (11.2x)**.  The relative path
also made them depend on prove's cwd, and like the first fifteen they ran on the
default 2 MB control stack instead of 512 MB.

=== THE WHOLE CHAIN, one full gate each, same tree, same 229 files / 7780 rows ===
    BEFORE (472f17c8, 224/7720, quiet box)   463 s wall   2933 CPU-s
    + lever A   (15 files)                   344          1983
    + lever A2  (10 files)                   164          1233
    + lever B   (the server, #1545)           86           395
  = 5.4x wall, 7.4x CPU.  Residue and the next lever: task #1546.
subject: The gate PROFILED per file (463 s / 2933 CPU-s), and the lever the table named: 15 files were recompiling the whole runtime on every row (974 -> 25.2 CPU-s)
